correctness.rationale: Strict concavity makes consecutive sample chords the upper boundary; each chord omits gap³/6 in one quadrant. The polar constraints indexed by a,b meet at w(a,b), where the slack for t is (t−a)(t−b)/(1+ab), so exactly the adjacent intersections give the quadrant boundary chain. The cut-off triangle at insertion has determinant magnitude (a−b)(a−c)(c−b)/D, reproduced independently (python /workspace/audit_checks/reconstruct.py 4); four triangles with the 1/2 area factor give q/D. The new primal is contained in the full parabolic lens and the old polar contains the disk: hence the claimed positive exchange lower bound. The full lens polar is found by maximizing tu+(1−t²)v on [0,1]; u_max is 1 up to v=1/2 and 2√(v(1−v)) thereafter. Thus the full polar area is 2+π/2. All bodies contain the fixed diamond, which justifies polar continuity for finite refinements and infinite prefixes with 0 adjoined. Strictness at the upper endpoint follows by one additional insertion in a positive gap before passing to the full lens; at the lower endpoint compare to the diamond or a finite three-knot subset. For a_n=r^n the interior knots are confined to [0,r] as r→0 and the maximum gap is 1−r as r→1, proving sharpness within the infinite class.
